summary: Brian Balfour opens by highlighting chaos in the AI product landscape — within 45 days, major companies launched numerous competing products across categories. Companies collapse in months rather than years (Chegg down 90%, Stack Overflow). He argues the critical question is 'What do I build and why will it win?' — always the job of product, now 10x harder. He compares the competitive environment to Gettysburg, with huge incumbents (Microsoft, Google, Meta), horizontal platforms (ChatGPT, Anthropic), monthly technology shifts, and hordes of startups including 5-6 per YC cohort. Balfour introduces Reforge's background: 10 years helping product teams, 100,000+ professionals, 400 experts, and a recent shift to encoding knowledge into AI agents (Reforge Insights as AI product researcher, Compass as project manager). He outlines two common traps: reinventing the AI wheel with custom models/infrastructure, and copy-pasting basic AI features like chatbots. The answer lies in treating AI as Lego blocks — assembling differentiated features by integrating best available AI capabilities with your unique assets. Three key Lego pieces: data (provides context for unique output, creates flywheel), functionality (controls AI behavior, gives superpowers), and understanding of unmet customer needs. Granola serves as case study: entered crowded AI note-taking market but found unmet need — help users take better notes rather than replacing note-taking. Used off-the-shelf capabilities but differentiated through unique data, functionality, and flywheel. Critically, Balfour emphasizes you cannot stop at initial assembly — you must sequence Lego blocks repeatedly, leveraging each layer into new unique combinations. Granola now offers team workspaces, CRM/HubSpot integrations, and auto-updating company wikis. Quoting Jamon Ball of Alterimator Capital: 'The real moat is just a sequence of smaller moats stacked together' — and where moats once lasted 6-12 months, today they buy only 2-3 weeks. Balfour closes by recapitulating the framework: identify unmet customer problems, find AI capabilities that solve them novelly, determine proprietary data and superpowers to give AI, then assemble and keep sequencing.
